dedupe_keys.name: pew research center internet broadband and technology survey datasets us

description: The Pew Research Center, through its Internet and Technology team and the earlier Pew Internet & American Life Project (from 2000), surveys American adults about internet access and use, home broadband adoption and the reasons people go without it, smartphone dependence, mobile use and online activities. The Center makes case-level microdata of much of its research available for secondary analysis after a period of time, listed by collection date on its datasets page, including American Trends Panel waves; older polls such as the Broadband Callback Survey are also archived at the Roper Center for Public Opinion Research. Coverage: the United States, national samples, 2000 to the present. Format and access: SPSS microdata with questionnaires and toplines, free of charge after creating a free account on the Pew website, under Pew's terms of use. Caveats: national samples of a few thousand adults at most, so no local detail; question wording changes over time. Simulation uses: shares of people who rely on home broadband or only on a smartphone, by age, income and place type, for social vulnerability and equity weighting of telecom outages. Related records: the NTIA Internet Use Survey gives larger official samples; FCC broadband data give supply.
